# Round 1md: structures generated by MD with the incomplete NEP

Rounds 0 and 1 built every training structure by hand: strain and rattle a
crystal, place an adatom at a fixed height, pack atoms at random. Round 1md
lets the current NEP make structures instead. It runs MD with that potential,
then sends a selected set of frames to VASP. There are two kinds of run:

- **Melt-quench.** A bulk cell is melted, quenched and annealed. It can then
  be cleaved and annealed again as a slab with vacuum. The amorphous AlN,
  SiNₓ, Al–Si and AlSiN phases that bad growth conditions produce come from
  these runs.
- **Collision.** Al, N, N₂ and Ar projectiles hit Si(111), AlN(0001),
  AlN(000-1) and the quenched amorphous slabs at 1–100 eV, one after another,
  so each impact lands on a surface that earlier impacts have already changed.

The potential is incomplete, and that is the reason to do this now. The MD goes
wherever this NEP takes deposition MD, including the places where the NEP is
wrong. Those places are exactly what the next training set needs. When the
MD visibly breaks (atoms collapse, energy runs away), the run stops. The
frames just before the failure are always sent to DFT.

"From round 1": the default potential is `round1wL_out/round1wL_nep.txt`, the
first one with all four types N Al Si Ar. The new data is merged into the
round-1wL dataset, and training continues round 1wL's `nep.restart`.

## Pipeline

| Step | Script | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `round1md_1_build_md_inputs.py` | One folder per MD run under `round1md_out/md/{quench,collision}/`. Runs on a login node in under a minute. |
| 2 | `round1md_2_anvil_lammps.sbatch` | LAMMPS array, one run per task, using `in.melt_quench.lmp` or `in.collision.lmp`. |
| 3 | `round1md_3_harvest.py` (+ `.sbatch`) | Screens the frames, selects about 900 and writes VASP folders with round 1's own writer. |
| 4 | `round1md_4_anvil_subVASP.sbatch` | VASP array. The job logic is round 1.5's restart-capable script, unchanged. |
| 5 | `round1md_5_build_dataset.sbatch` | Builds the new frames into a dataset, writes the NEP-vs-DFT report (`round1md_6_nep_vs_dft.py`), and merges with round 1wL. |
| 6 | `round1md_nep.sbatch` + `round1md_nep-1.in` | Continues round 1wL's training on the merged set. Same architecture. |

Run everything from `rounds/` (the project root):

```bash
module load conda; module use $HOME/privatemodules; module load conda-env/nepdata
python round1md_code/round1md_1_build_md_inputs.py --nep round1wL_out/round1wL_nep.txt
LMP_BIN=/path/to/lmp bash round1md_code/round1md_run_md.sh          # steps 2-3
# read round1md_out/vasp/harvest_report.txt, then
bash round1md_code/round1md_generateVASP_trainNEP.sh                # steps 4-6
```

Once the quench runs have finished, collisions on the amorphous slabs can be
added. The builder never touches existing run folders, and the LAMMPS array
skips runs that are already finished:

```bash
python round1md_code/round1md_1_build_md_inputs.py --only collision --targets none \
    --amorphous-targets 'round1md_out/md/quench/*/slab_final.data'
LMP_BIN=/path/to/lmp bash round1md_code/round1md_run_md.sh
```

**LAMMPS needs `pair_style nep`.** Build LAMMPS with NEP_CPU's `USER-NEP`
package (https://github.com/brucefan1983/NEP_CPU, `interface/lammps/`). Stock
modules do not include it. The inputs use the current syntax:
`pair_style nep` / `pair_coeff * * nep.txt N Al Si Ar`. Atom types follow the
element order of `nep.txt`.

## The melt-quench (`in.melt_quench.lmp`)

The bulk cell is quenched first, then vacuum is optionally added. All stages
run at fixed volume (NVT). A density scan over run folders takes the place of
NPT, because an incomplete potential can collapse or blow apart an NPT cell.

| Stage | Ensemble | Dump |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relax | `nve/limit` + Langevin at 300 K for 1 ps. Removes the close contacts of the random packing. | none |
| melt | NVT at T_melt for 20 ps | `dump.melt.lammpstrj` |
| quench | NVT ramp from T_melt to 300 K at 50 or 10 K/ps | `dump.quench.lammpstrj` |
| anneal | NVT at 300 K for 10 ps | `dump.anneal.lammpstrj`, `bulk_final.data` |
| slab (`--vacuum` > 0) | Shift by a random `zshift`, add 12 Å of vacuum, heat to 900 K, hold, cool to 300 K | `dump.slab.lammpstrj`, `slab_final.data` |

Compositions (`QUENCH_SYSTEMS` in the builder; ~96 atoms each), each at 0.92,
1.00 and 1.08 × the listed density:

| System | Why | Density g/cm³ | T_melt K |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AlN, Al₃N₂, Al₂N₃ | a-AlN, Al-rich and N-rich films (N₂ forms in Al₂N₃) | 3.0 / 2.9 / 2.8 | 3500 / 3000 / 3500 |
| Si | a-Si | 2.3 | 2500 |
| Si₃N₄, SiN, Si₂N | the SiNₓ that forms when N reaches bare Si | 3.0 / 2.8 / 2.6 | 3500 / 3200 / 3000 |
| AlSi, Al₃Si | Al–Si liquid and amorphous phases (Al pre-deposition) | 2.45 | 2200 / 2000 |
| AlSiN₂ | an intermixed interface layer | 3.0 | 3500 |
| AlN + 3% Ar | Ar trapped in a sputtered film (only if the NEP has Ar) | 2.95 | 3500 |

The densities are rough amorphous or liquid values to start from, not fitted
numbers. The scan is there because the potential has to see a range of
densities anyway.

## The collisions (`in.collision.lmp`)

- **Targets.** Si(111), Al-polar AlN(0001) and N-polar AlN(000-1), each
  4 × 4 × 4 bilayers (128 atoms). The quenched amorphous slabs can be added
  as targets too. The crystalline slabs are cut between bilayers, so each
  surface atom has one dangling bond. The builder checks this (see the first
  finding below).
- **Layers.** The bottom bilayer is fixed. Above it is a Langevin bath at
  T_sub (300 or 900 K). The top of the slab and every projectile run NVE, so
  the impact itself is not thermostatted.
- **Impacts.** There are 8 per run. For each one, species, aim point and
  azimuth are drawn at random. Energy is one of 1, 5, 10, 20, 50 or 100 eV,
  and the polar angle is 0° or 45°. The projectile starts at r_c + 2 Å above
  the surface, outside the NEP cutoff. N₂ is a rigid molecule at its gas bond
  length, randomly oriented, and its energy is that of the whole molecule.
- **Time step.** `fix dt/reset` keeps every atom under 0.04 Å per step, so a
  100 eV N projectile runs at about 0.1 fs and the thermalised surface at the
  maximum (0.5 fs with N present).
- **Dumps.** Every 10 steps for 1500 steps around each impact, then 40 frames
  over 2 ps of relaxation.

## Screening and selection (`round1md_3_harvest.py`)

For each frame, the contact ratio is the smallest d_ij / (r_cov,i + r_cov,j)
over all pairs.

| Check | Default | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| contact ratio < keep ratio | 0.60 quench, 0.50 collision | frame not used |
| contact ratio < 0.40 | collapse | this frame and every later frame of the run are discarded. A collision is exempt during the impact itself (a 100 eV hit does reach ~0.8 Å), but not if the contact survives into relaxation |
| NEP max \|F\| | > 50 (quench) / 300 (collision) eV/Å | frame not used |
| projectile still > 4 Å from the surface | | frame not used (it is just the slab) |
| last 3 good frames before a collapse or `fix halt` | | always selected |

Slab frames lose any atom or molecule that is more than 4 Å from the slab and
get 12 Å of vacuum. With ISPIN = 1, a lone N or Al atom would also get the
wrong spin state.

Selection is farthest-point sampling in a pair-distance-histogram
descriptor, with these budgets per stage:

| Bucket | Frames | Split |
| --- | --- | --- |
| amorphous_bulk | 300 | melt 30%, quench 50%, anneal 20% |
| amorphous_slab | 150 | |
| collision | 450 | impact 60%, relaxation 40% |

A per-run cap keeps any one run from dominating. Collision frames are
described only by the atoms the impacts changed: projectiles, plus target
atoms that have moved more than 1 Å. Otherwise the 128 unchanged slab atoms
would make every collision frame look the same. The round-1wL training set
seeds the bulk/slab sampling, so frames that look like data already there are
picked last.

The VASP folders use round 1's `write_vasp_tree`, so everything matches the
campaign: ENCUT = 1.3 × the largest ENMAX, k-spacing 0.25 Å⁻¹, the dipole
correction on cells with vacuum, and ISPIN = 1 for condensed cells. The NEP
energy and forces of every selected frame go to `selected_nep.extxyz`. After
VASP, `round1md_6_nep_vs_dft.py` reports the round-1 NEP's error per bucket
and stage on exactly the structures its own MD produced.

## Compared with the round 0/1 adsorption and displaced structures

The generators of round 0 and round 1 (`generate_round0.py`,
`generate_round1.py`) use the same algorithms; round 1 only triples the
counts. I ran `generate_round1.py` locally without POTCARs and measured what
it produces.

### Adsorption bucket (`gen_adsorption`)

What it does:

- Al or N single adatoms at the top, bridge and hollow sites of a 2 × 2
  Si(111) slab. There are 6 heights per site (1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.6, 3.4 and
  4.5 Å), 12 frames each.
- Random 2–5-atom clusters.
- Ordered and random coverages from 0.25 to 1 ML.
- Points along a straight line between two sites, as stand-ins for
  diffusion paths.

All of it is static, and the substrate sits frozen at its ideal positions.

Limitations, and what the collisions add:

1. **The substrate never responds.** A real adatom pulls its neighbours,
   breaks or forms bonds, and pushes surface atoms down. In a static scan the
   only thing that changes is the adatom height. A collision run produces the
   approach, the impact, the substrate's response and then the relaxed bound
   state. The bound state is what the static scan was trying to guess.
2. **The heights are not physical.** 1.0 Å above a top site puts Al–Si in the
   ZBL range (ratio 0.43 in the generated set). It is expensive to converge in
   DFT and teaches the NEP nothing it does not already have from ZBL. In a
   collision the closest approach is set by the kinetic energy, so the
   repulsive wall is sampled only as far as 1–100 eV atoms actually reach.
3. **The Si(111) slab has the wrong termination.** `ase.build.surface` (and
   `diamond111`, which `scripts/aln_si_structures.py` uses) cuts through the
   bilayers. Every top and bottom Si atom has coordination 1, which means
   three dangling bonds. The real bulk-terminated surface has one. All
   round 0/1 adsorption, slab_Si and interface structures sit on this
   high-energy surface. The collision targets are cut between bilayers, and
   the builder checks that every surface atom has coordination 3.
4. **Only Si is ever a substrate.** Adsorption on AlN, the growth front once
   the first layer is down, is not sampled at all. The collisions use both
   AlN polarities, plus amorphous surfaces.
5. **Ar is missing**, and Ar is the dominant energetic species in sputtering.
   Here it is a projectile.
6. **Same seed, deterministic scan.** Round 1 repeats 48 of round 0's 300
   adsorption structures exactly (`rounds/README.md`). MD with fresh random
   impacts does not repeat itself.

What the collisions do **not** replace: the static scan maps the energy
along the height at each site, and short MD will rarely cross a diffusion
barrier in a few picoseconds. Both matter for validation step 3 (adsorption
energies and barriers). Keep a small static set, but from 1.8 Å upward, on a
correctly terminated slab, and use NEB for the barriers.

### Displaced structures (rattle, compressed rattle, disordered, interface)

What the generator does:

- Gaussian displacements of every atom, independent of each other.
  - bulk: σ 0.02–0.22 Å
  - slabs: σ 0.03–0.20 Å
  - interface: σ 0.04–0.15 Å
  - `compressed_rattle`: σ 0.20–0.50 Å, in cells compressed by 8–30%
  - `amorphous_interlayer`: σ 0.25–0.45 Å, within ±2–4 Å of the interface
- Random packings at 0.75–1.12 × the crystal density.
- A random film placed on a slab.
- Atoms swapped across the interface.

Limitations, measured on the generated set:

1. **Independent random displacements are not thermal motion.** In MD,
   neighbouring atoms move together (phonons), so bond lengths stay within
   what the temperature allows. Independent displacements of 0.3–0.5 Å
   shorten many bonds at once. The median contact ratio is 0.53 for
   `compressed_rattle` (Si–Si at 1.15 Å) and 0.44 for `amorphous_interlayer`.
   The melt-quench frames reach the same temperatures with correlated
   displacements: a-AlN annealed at 300 K has a median ratio of 0.83.
2. **A random packing is not an amorphous solid.** In the round-1
   `random_packing` AlN cells, 53% of first-neighbour Al/N bonds are Al–Al or
   N–N. In the melt-quenched a-AlN it is 14%: Al–N alternation survives
   melting and quenching. The potential needs the second kind, because that
   is what a badly grown film looks like.
3. **`disordered_film_on_slab` has an overlap in every frame.** All 37
   generated frames have an Al–Al pair at about 0.90 Å; the Al–Al bond is
   2.86 Å. The placement check compares every pair with one threshold,
   `0.85 * min(mind_all.values())`, which is the N–N value. Bulk
   `interstitial` frames (ratio 0.47) and adsorption `cluster` frames (down to
   0.35) have the same problem. Round 1wL already had to drop round 1.7's
   `disordered` bucket for SCF blow-ups.
4. **The interface film is sheared: Al–N pairs at 1.19 Å.**
   - In every round 0/1 interface structure, even the unrattled `registry`
     and `separation` scans, 50 Al–N pairs in the AlN film are 1.19 Å apart.
     The bulk bond is 1.89 Å.
   - Cause: the lattice match pairs the 60° Si(111) supercell with a 120°
     AlN supercell. `build_interface` then maps the film onto the substrate
     cell with `set_cell(..., scale_atoms=True)`, which shears the atoms inside
     the cell even though the lattice points coincide.
   - Fix: change the film's basis to 60° (b → a + b) before mapping.
   - It may be part of why every round-0 interface folder needed
     resubmission. I listed it under Known issues in `rounds/README.md` and
     did not change the round code, which is kept as it was run.
5. **No crystallographic dislocations.** The interface is a coherent
   16:25 coincidence cell. The misfit dislocations that relax AlN on Si need
   cells far too large for VASP. Neither the old generator nor this round
   covers them. A later round could run NEP MD on a large interface and cut
   the dislocation cores out as DFT-sized clusters.

What replaces them here:

- Melt, quench and anneal give displaced structures at the amplitude each
  temperature and chemistry actually produce, from 4000 K liquid down to a
  300 K glass, at three densities.
- Collision thermal spikes create vacancies, interstitials, implanted Ar and
  locally molten regions the way deposition does.

For later rounds:

- Keep the small crystal rattles (σ ≤ 0.1 Å), which probe the curvature near
  equilibrium.
- Drop `compressed_rattle` above σ 0.3, `amorphous_interlayer` and
  `disordered_film_on_slab`.
- Fix the interface shear before generating more interface structures.

### What this round still lacks

The selection uses structural novelty and failure detection, not model
uncertainty, because there is only one model. Round 1.7 and round 1wL have
the same types (N Al Si Ar). If both potentials are kept, the force
disagreement between them on the harvested frames would be a better selection
score. It could be added to `round1md_3_harvest.py` as a second ranking.

## Testing

This round was tested locally with LAMMPS 22 Jul 2025 and NEP_CPU built as a
plugin. NEP89 (`nep89_20250409`, which covers N, Al, Si and Ar) stood in for
`round1wL_nep.txt`, which is not in the repository.

- Short melt-quench runs (AlN, Si₃N₄, Si, AlN + Ar) went through every stage,
  including the cleave and the slab anneal.
- Collision runs on Si(111), AlN(0001), AlN(000-1) and two quenched amorphous
  slabs finished. Projectiles cross the surface plane within 0.2 Å of their
  aim point.
- NEP89 never failed. To test the failure path, I set the `d_halt` and
  `--collapse-ratio` thresholds artificially strict. The halt stopped the run
  and its last frames were selected as pre-failure.
- The SLURM scripts were run with stub `sbatch`/`module`/`mpirun`, so the
  chunking, dependencies, the DONE/HALTED markers and the restart/scratch/resume
  logic of the NEP job were all exercised. They have not been run on Anvil.
- NEP_CPU ran at about 9 × 10³ atom-steps/s per core. A 96-atom quench at
  10 K/ps is about 7 × 10⁵ steps, which is 1–2 h on 8 cores. The harvest
  takes about 10 ms per frame.
